question: to the Commission Krzysztof Brejza (PPE) Subject:

Recent reports indicate that Russian SIM cards are being utilised as tools for military and intelligence operations. According to Ukrainian officials, these cards enable Russian forces to guide drones and missiles with high precision by using local cellular infrastructure and roaming services, as well as EU roaming close to the EU border. Furthermore, they enable the bypassing of Western sanctions on Russian digital services and communication tracking. In the light of these security concerns: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the specific role Russian SIM cards play in coordinating military strikes and enabling hybrid warfare activities within the EU and its neighbourhood?

Does the Commission have a comprehensive strategy for countering these Russian tactics, such as implementing an EU-wide ban on Russian SIM cards or terminating all remaining roaming agreements with Russian telecommunications providers to step up collective security?
Since the Russian Federation has already blocked network access for millions of SIM cards from EU Member States, why has the EU not yet taken equivalent steps?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.9.2026) The European Commission has presented an EU Action Plan on Drone and Counter Drone Security1 for a united approach against threats posed by malicious drones. The Action plan presents practical solutions for improved prevention of incidents, detection of drones, response to malicious drone activities and strengthening Europe’s defence readiness against drone threats. Under the European Electronic Communications Code2, Member States’ authorities are able to require providers of public electronic communications networks or publicly available electronic communications services to block, but only on a case-by-case basis, access to numbers or services where this is justified by reasons of fraud or misuse and to require that in such cases providers of electronic communications services withhold relevant interconnection or other service revenues.
1 COM/2026/81 final, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026DC0081. 2 Directive (EU) 2018/1972 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018 establishing

the European Electronic Communications Code, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2018/1972/oj; Article 97(2): Member States shall ensure that national regulatory or other competent authorities are able to require providers of public electronic communications networks or publicly available electronic communications services to block, on a case- by-case basis, access to numbers or services where this is justified by reasons of fraud or misuse and to require that in such cases providers of electronic communications services withhold relevant interconnection or other service revenues.
